analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/hardware-support.md: a date bump (line 3), a new KV re-slice floor paragraph (head lines 559-574), a revised invariant 6 (head lines 850-853), and a new failure-mode row (head line 867). The unit text contained no executable code, so I inspected the documentation's claims against the threat model.

The documented behavior is a provider-local availability and memory-accounting change: `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` now honors per-slot `minimumServiceableGrantBytes` floors. It refuses a load or reserve raise when the floors sum above the fleet KV budget, and `resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor` rejects the `Int.max` sentinel. The description states that unreserved memory, activation floors, and the process ledger remain authoritative, and that regrowth after unload or rollback never shrinks a slot below its floor. I found nothing that weakens these controls. Related threats are T-016, T-029 and T-041, plus A-018 availability.

The docs mention no change to encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization, coordinator trust, prefix-cache at-rest posture, or any wire field. The prefix-cache text (T-041 and SEC-035) is unchanged. The statement that a newcomer loaded last can still fail with `no_kv_headroom` is fail-closed, so it does not widen any grant.

I could not verify that the underlying source changes (`resliceGrants`, `resliceAndBuildEngineV2Bundle`, `resliceGrowSurvivorsLocked`, `EngineV2Bridge.requireServiceableOrdinaryGrant`) match this documentation, because they were not supplied. The patch excerpt is also truncated. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression. No finding qualifies, and no threat-model update is required for this documentation-only change.
